82_marg1543: From what Scriptures he took this testimony does not appear. But allegorically it is plain. The body of Moses: the people of Israel, because Moses was a part of that people; and therefore what is read in Zacharias to have been done about the people, the Apostle perhaps rightly says was done about the body of Moses. In Zacharias it is read: “The Lord shewed me Jesus the high priest standing before the angel of the Lord: and Satan stood on his right hand to be his adversary,” and the Lord said to Satan: “The Lord rebuke thee, O Satan: and the Lord that chose Jerusalem rebuke thee.” Because Jesus the priest desired that Israel be freed from captivity and return into their own land, Satan resisted him, unwilling that the people be freed, but wishing them to be enslaved to the Gentile enemies. Therefore the angel who was the helper of the people rebuked him and removed him from the injury of the people. But wherever or whenever this altercation of the angel with the devil took place, this is to be carefully observed: that if Michael the archangel would not speak railing speech against the devil who opposed him, but restrained him with modest speech, how much more must all railing be avoided by men, and most of all against the Creator. The devil is good in substance but evil in will, and therefore he is not railed at by the angel, because the archangel reckons it railing to bring anything against a good nature; and if the devil’s nature were evil, the Lord would not rebuke him for a good work, which could not exist in an evil nature. But when the Lord rebukes, he shows that something good can proceed from a good nature.
82_marg1544: It can be supposed that the angel carried on a dispute with the devil about the body of Moses, as if he were unwilling that the burial of Moses be revealed to the Jews, lest they adore him as a god, which the devil was trying to bring about; but it is not found in authority.
82_marg1545: It is read otherwise: that the Lord hid the body of Moses, and perhaps for this reason, lest the people of Israel, after the manner of the Gentiles, who worshipped as gods the kings and princes who were friends to them, after their deaths, their statues having been made, should adore the body of Moses and by idolatry of this kind transgress against God. One can therefore see that there was as it were a contest and altercation of Michael with the devil, who wished to reveal the body of Moses, that he might deceive the people by idolatry, while Michael forbade it, lest the people whose prince he was should sin. And although this is never read in the Old Testament, yet on account of the authority of the apostle, who knew certain more secret things which are hidden from us, it ought not to be refuted by anyone.
